issue.title: Bound historical rowless proc logs under the log owner
issue.description: Proposed by sase-zw.8.2 note #1; independently verified by sase-zw.8.land at main 00acd607f on 2026-09-14. Canonical ~/.sase/procs/logs contains 459 regular nonsymlink <proc-id>.log files absent from all 103 durable proc rows: 60063 bytes, oldest mtime about 31.9 days. Earlier phase saw 456. Current procs/store.py only calls delete_proc_logs for rows newly pruned; the runtime orphan sweep intentionally covers runtime directories, so historical logs never reach an owner cleanup. Investigate provenance and implement safe bounded log-owner reconciliation if appropriate, preserving active/reserved and producer-owned logs plus rotation/lock lifetimes. Do not infer deletion authorization from this report. Read-only reproduction uses proc_logs_dir(), read_proc_snapshot(), and compares glob("*.log") stems with all snapshot proc_id values, then sums stat sizes. Semantic searches across every task type/status plus the last-week sweep found no duplicate. Active rename/typed-launch epics were reviewed; historical orphan log lifetime predates sase-s6 and no causal connection to a rename was established. This is distinct from sase-zw.8 runtime safety repair and sase-104 fleet payload minimization.

task_type_fields.impact: Historical proc log count is unbounded despite row/runtime retention. Current measured byte cost is small, so prioritize safe ownership and lifetime analysis over immediate deletion.
task_type_fields.repro: Compare regular nonsymlink *.log filename stems in proc_logs_dir() to all proc_id values from read_proc_snapshot(); current host has 459 rowless logs (60063 bytes, up to 31.9 days old) that row-prune-only cleanup cannot visit.
